subject: CSC
label: Grade 10
task: Meet the outcome of every unit in Grade 10 Computer science, and keep one piece of evidence for each.
condition: A 36-week school year, 4 units, a teacher or guide, a learning book or device, and local examples in the local language first with English support.
standard: Each unit: at least 8 of 10 marks on a short task, with one line of reasoning for each answer. Course pass: no unit at 'Not yet' after one retry, and a pass in SA1 and SA2.

modules.title: Python: functions, files and data structures
modules.outcome: write programs using lists, dictionaries and files
modules.intro: In this unit you work on 'Python: functions, files and data structures', taught in a way that is with notes, a worked line and a self-mark. The target is clear: write programs using lists, dictionaries and files. You move from seeing it, to saying it, to doing it alone.
points: See it: watch or try the skill in 'Python: functions, files and data structures' on a teacher screen or a safe device.
Name the parts: write the key words and what each part does.
Use it: write programs using lists, dictionaries and files. Save your work in a named file or folder.
Test and fix: run it, find one fault, correct it, and note what you changed.
modules.example: Model run for 'Python: functions, files and data structures'. Goal in one sentence. Plan: list the steps in order before touching the device. Do: follow the plan, saving after each step. Test: try normal input and one unusual input. Fix: change one thing and test again. Share: show a partner and explain it. What a good answer looks like: it works for normal input, steps match the plan, and the learner can explain each part. Online safety rules apply at all times.
modules.activity: About 30 to 40 minutes of class work, then one short practice task for home. Keep evidence: a worked task and a corrected copy.
modules.standard: Write programs using lists, dictionaries and files: at least 8 of 10 marks on a short task, with one line of reasoning for each answer.

When do the formative checks FA1 to FA4 and the summative checks SA1 and SA2 happen?
FA1 to FA4 around weeks 6, 12, 24 and 30; SA1 in week 18; SA2 in week 36.
In which weeks does Unit 4 (Cyber law and ethics) run?
What evidence do you keep for each unit, and why?
A worked task and a corrected copy. It shows what you can really do and lets a teacher check it against the standard.
ladder: L1: use a device safely; click, type and draw.
L2: create documents; follow simple instructions in blocks.
L3: spreadsheets, algorithms and simple programs.
L5: software design, databases and security.
L7 (postgraduate): research, architecture or AI practice.
